newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-EDBERG BEATS STICH IN PARIS OPEN FIRST ROUND.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-EDBERG BEATS STICH IN PARIS OPEN FIRST ROUND.

text.p: Stefan Edberg, who is retiring at the end of the season, trounced Michael Stich in straight sets in the first round of the Paris Open on Monday.
The 30-year-old Swede took one hour and 19 minutes to beat the German 6-2 6-4. Both men were former Wimbledon champions.

Edberg, whose world ranking of 17 left him one place outside the seedings in a tournamant boasting most of the top 30, faces number three Thomas Muster of Austria in the second round when all the seeds enter the fray.
He played immaculate serve and volley tennis as he reeled off five successive games to go 5-1 up in the opening set.
Stich, in contrast, was some way off the stylish game that helped him reach the final of this year's French Open
The world number 20 had an angry exchange with the umpire after an apparent fault by Edberg was ruled good, denying the German a break point.
Stich told the umpire: "Let's make a deal. After the match, I'll come to your office and we'll check that ball on the video. If I'm right you don't climb into a chair again."
The umpire ignored him and Stich went on to lose the set 6-2 in 38 minutes.
The second set was much tighter, but Edberg came up with an answer to all seven break points that Stich had in four successive games.
The Swede, dominant at the net, broke Stich again and took the match on his serve.
"I always like playing in Paris," said Edberg. "The atmosphere is great here and the people love my tennis. I'm just sorry I never won (the French Open at) Roland Garros."
